definition.simple: The total path you traveled, no matter which way you went.
definition.academic: The total length of the actual path covered by an object in motion.

examples: Walking 5km on a treadmill (your distance is 5km, even though you didn't go anywhere).

common_misconceptions: Thinking distance is always a straight line.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask them if their smartwatch counts distance even if they run in circles.

definition.simple: The straight-line shortcut from where you started to where you ended up, including the direction.
definition.academic: The shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final position of an object, along with its direction.

examples: Going 3km East and 4km North results in a displacement of 5km North-East.

common_misconceptions: Believing displacement can be larger than distance.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Have them draw a triangle. Distance is the two sides, displacement is the hypotenuse.

definition.simple: Speed with a direction. Like '50 km/h North'.
definition.academic: The rate of change of displacement of an object with respect to time.

examples: A car driving 100 km/h on a highway going East.

common_misconceptions: Thinking velocity and speed are exactly the same thing.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask what happens if two cars have the same speed but different velocities.

definition.simple: How quickly you speed up, slow down, or change direction.
definition.academic: The rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.

examples: Pressing the gas pedal in a car.
Slamming on the brakes (negative acceleration or deceleration).

common_misconceptions: Thinking you are accelerating when going at a constant fast speed.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Remind them that turning the steering wheel is also acceleration!
